senses.gloss: m.(b. h.; cmp. כְּרַב I; v. , however, Schr. KAT2 p. 39; p. 609) [head,] Cherub.
units: Succ. 5ᵇ; Ḥag. 13ᵇ … מאי כ׳ כרַבְיָא וכ׳ what is K’rub?—… ‘Childlike’, for in Babylonia they call a child rabia.
<cite ref="Chagigah 13b:6">Ib.</cite> <he>והפכו לכ׳</he> and he changed it (the face of the ox, <cite ref="Ezekiel 1:10">Ez. I, 10</cite>) into that of a Cherub.
<cite ref="Ezekiel 1:10">Ib.</cite> <he>היינו פני כ׳ וכ׳</he> the face of the Ch. is the same as that of man, the one being large, the other small.
<cite ref="Vayikra Rabbah 32">Lev. R. s. 32</cite>; a. e.—Pl. <he>כְּרוּבִים</he>. Tanḥ. ed. Bub.

<cite ref="Genesis 25">B’resh. 25</cite> <he>לפיכן נקראו כ׳ שהן רבים</he> (read: <cite ref="T00306"><he>רוֹבִים</he></cite>, v. <cite ref="T00301"><he>רוֹבֶה</he></cite>) they are called Ch., because they are young (childlike), v. supra.
<cite ref="Yoma 54b:1">Yoma 54ᵇ</cite> <he>מעורים וכ׳ הכ׳ ראה</he> saw the figures of the cherubs twined around each other.
<cite ref="Yoma 54a:17">Ib. 54ᵃ</cite> <he>כ׳ דצורתא וכ׳</he> painted cherubs were in the Second Temple; a. e.
